title: `objectstack validate` passes a flow whose try_catch catch region has several sinks; the engine refuses it at registration ("region must be single-exit") with only a WARN, so the flow never runs
body:
Filed by the objectstack-ai/duly lane seat from a measurement on duly (objectstack-ai/duly#160, PR objectstack-ai/duly#163). For central triage; no `domain:*` label is set here.

## What happens (@objectstack 18.2.0)

A flow whose `try_catch` catch region ends in several sinks, for example a `decision` fanning out to three `notify` nodes with no join, passes `objectstack validate` (exit 0) and `objectstack build`.

At kernel registration the automation engine refuses the same flow: "region must be single-exit". It logs this only at WARN, the boot continues, and the flow is never registered, so its trigger never fires. Nothing in the author-time gates or in the boot's exit status tells the author.

Measured twice by the duly card thread: once while building, and again by removing the join node from the final shape.

## Expected

The single-exit rule the engine enforces is enforced at author time, in `validate` and `build` (spec or lint), with the same message. A flow the engine will refuse should not pass the gate that exists to catch it. Separately, triage may want a registration refusal to be louder than a WARN, for example by counting in the boot summary as a binding failure.

Dedupe words: try_catch single-exit region, flow registration refused WARN, validate passes engine refuses flow.
